threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You keep trying to pay for your coffee with cash at the hipster cafes. They look at you like you just walked in from the 90s.
Last night on the 333, a guy argued with the driver over the fare while a woman sang Adele. Only in Brixton would you get that mix.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I spotted my neighbor feeding a street cat while arguing with a pigeon—classic Neukölln, right? Only here you find harmony in the chaos.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg will you find a kebab shop that doubles as an art gallery, serving late-night snacks while showcasing local talent on the walls.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from here when they say 'Civic Center' without flinching at the chaos, like it’s just another Tuesday.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 5 bus today during peak hours—it was standing room only and someone brought a karaoke machine. Only in the Tenderloin.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists miss that the real vibe of Gràcia comes alive after dark—it's when the squares fill with locals, laughing and sharing tapas, not during the day.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new by the way they navigate through the streets, looking up at the buildings instead of watching where they're walking.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still queue for food at Dalston Superstore like it’s a restaurant, instead of fighting for a spot at the bar like the rest of us.
Caught the 45 last night; a guy at the back was knitting a bright pink scarf while blasting old school garage. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a kid riding a scooter past a street musician serenading a stray cat by the donut shop on Hermannstraße.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you stumble across a late-night kebab stand that doubles as a gallery, showcasing local artists while you wait for your döner.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their contempt for BART's endless delays—like clockwork, they already have a backup plan involving the J-Church.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 49 this morning—driver sung along to the radio like he was headlining a concert. Surreal and oddly uplifting vibe for a Tuesday commute.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia's busy plazas are just for leisure; they're actually community hubs where locals gossip and swap news daily.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones still trying to navigate the T-10 metro card, confused as locals breeze through like it’s second nature.
